name: Jaala
title: Descendant of Solomon's Servants
summary: Jaala (also spelled Jaala/Jaali) was the ancestor of a family of descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem. The family is mentioned in the lists of those who returned with Zerubbabel. Jaala represents the faithful families that preserved their identity through the exile and participated in the rebuilding of the Jewish community.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the descendants of Solomon's servants in the book of Ezra
keyEvents.description: Jaala's family is listed among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the descendants of Solomon's servants in the book of Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: Jaala's descendants are again listed in Nehemiah's parallel list of those who returned from the exile, here spelled 'Jaala'.

keyEvents.title: The Return from Babylon
keyEvents.description: Jaala's family was among the many who followed Zerubbabel back to Judah from the Babylonian exile, marking an important era in Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: The role of Solomon's servants in temple service
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Solomon's servants, including the family of Jaala, were counted among the temple servants (Nethinim) and had special duties related to the temple.
